name: Weitan Waifu patch
short: Applied to the skin. One 120-person trial after cancer surgery: 3 adverse events among 60 on the patch (5%), including mild to moderate skin peeling, itching and nausea; they settled after stopping.
text: Weitan Waifu patch is a Chinese medicine applied to the skin, not taken by mouth; in the only trial found it was stuck on two acupuncture points (Zhongwan and Shenque) for 14 days or until the effective standard was reached. In that multicentre, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial in 120 people with gastroparesis after surgery for gastrointestinal cancer, 3 adverse events were recorded among the 60 people with the patch (an incidence the abstract gives as 5.0%, 3 of 60), including mild to moderate skin peeling (decrustation), itching and nausea, which went away after the patch was stopped; the difference from the placebo group was not significant. The abstract says no severe adverse events were seen in the placebo group but does not give that group's number of adverse events, and it does not say what the patch contains. No interaction data were found in the cited source.
